- If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.6) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast peak values by 2–5%.
- If sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.4) or volatile, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 2–5% to compensate for downward bias.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true by >5%), model overreacts; cap next 3–5 days’ forecast at 10–15% below peak.
- If true price moves sharply downward after a forecast peak, model fails to mean-revert; adjust forecast to align with recent 5–7 day average.
- When sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.3–0.7), model often misjudges trend direction; favor 3–5 day moving average over 30d forecast.
- If forecast is consistently higher than true for 3+ consecutive days, apply downward correction proportional to sentiment decay (e.g., 0.8x if sentiment drops below 0.5).
- If forecast is consistently lower than true for 3+ consecutive days, apply upward correction proportional to sentiment rise (e.g., 1.2x if sentiment >0.7).
